Its expected band gap is above 2 eV, so it should be insulating.

A borate with no reducible or easily oxidized cation, and a high Li content that should match the electrolyte's Li chemistry, might give a lower contact penalty. This family has not been tested yet.

proposals.hypothesis: LiF is a wide-gap, Li-rich, electronically insulating fluoride with no reducible or easily oxidized cation. Its only contact-relevant anion is F-, which resists oxidation at 4.0 V. The fluoride series (Li3AlF6, LiMgAlF6, LiCaAlF6) gave the lowest penalties so far, and their contact products were dominated by metal-fluoride products (AlF3, MgF2, CaAlF5) plus P/S/Cl species. Pure LiF has no Al/Mg/Ca cation to form those metal-fluoride products, so it may give a lower contact penalty.
proposals.motivation: LiCaAlF6 (mp-aaaaajby) was the best candidate so far (0.048 eV/non-Li atom, bin 2, acceptable), and the fluoride family was the only one with penalties below 0.1 eV. Its remaining contact products were metal fluorides (CaAlF5) plus PF5, S and SCl. Testing LiF checks whether removing the trivalent/divalent metal fluoride channel lowers the penalty further.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate that is widely used as a protective coating between oxide cathodes and sulfide electrolytes. Its phosphate chemistry should be reasonably compatible with Li6PS5Cl and with LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, and it should limit interfacial space-charge and decomposition. This is a first, unexplored family, so it serves as a baseline probe.

LiCl is a wide-gap (~9 eV), electronically insulating, Li-rich halide. It shares the chloride anion with Li6PS5Cl, so it should have little driving force to react with the argyrodite electrolyte, and it is fairly oxidation-resistant at 4.0 V vs Li. This tests whether a halide family gives a much smaller contact penalty than the phosphate baseline (0.337 eV/atom, not acceptable).
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) gave status ok and insulating, but its contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom (bin 16) was far above the 0.05 eV acceptability threshold, mainly from decomposition into P2O5, SCl4 and SO2 at the electrolyte contact. This motivates switching to a different chemistry that avoids oxidative sulfur and phosphorus products.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is the canonical oxide buffer for sulfide-electrolyte/oxide-cathode interfaces. Nb5+ is hard to reduce, so it should resist reduction by the argyrodite and limit P/S oxidation at the LiCoO2 side at 4.0 V. Earlier phosphate (0.337 eV) and chloride (0.408 eV) coatings both gave sulfur/phosphorus oxidation products, so an oxide with a high-valence transition-metal cation should be a different and potentially lower-penalty chemistry. Its expected band gap is above 2 eV, so it should be insulating.
